doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Childhood, schooling and the New York band scene
title: Picking up instruments and not knowing strings
summary: He learned the mechanics of instruments by fooling around with them, but knows nothing about playing strings and writes for them by ear.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Was that in a school situation or on your own, where you learned all this?
Both. Both. Not in a school situation, no, I’d just pick up peoples instruments and start fooling around with them, trying to see what the physics were and all that, the mechanics.
Were you somebody like say, a Johnny Richards who eventually got at least a working skill on just about every instrument?
Well… enough, you know, not strings; I don’t know anything about strings what-so­ ever.
Except how to write for them?

I really, yeah, but I don’t know what it feels like to play a part, I’ve heard enough good string writing that I can, I can ape it, you know, and I know they can make impossible skips that you can’t do on wind instruments and things like that. But when I write I scarcely plumb what the string player is capable of. I just try to write enough so they don’t get bored.
That’s probably the key to success, wouldn’t you say?
[Laughs] You just keep string players from playing footballs.
